title: Nine months in Chicago and the birth of jazz
summary: In Chicago the band added syncopation to a one step, the crowd demanded jazz, and the name was added to the band.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Nine months. We were there nine months. It was in Chicago that I assumed we were going to be a flop, and I said to the boys, let me swing one of those things that we played in the carnival parades and put some syncopation to it. I see they're doing a one step here. I used to dance very well.
And we tried one, and the people hollered, and they hollered, give us more jazz. In less than a week, they had the police and firemen to come out there.
Now, tell me this, Nick. In other words, when you first went to Chicago, then the band wasn't playing jazz there either.
No, no. We hadn't changed the rhythm there.
In other words, the band went up there more...
We developed it there by watching these people who were trying to imitate Vine and Castle doing the castle walk, which was a one step.
I see. So in other words, you didn't even leave New Orleans as a jazz band. You went up there as actually a dance band.
The word I never heard before in my life until I ate Chicago.
And that's when the word jazz was born.
That's right. And Harry James picked that up, and he added it to the name.
And he called us the original Dixieland jazz band because after our success there, brought many boys from New Orleans. And every band was calling himself a New Orleans jazz band.
